hypnogram.source: decoded - see the `decoding` block. NOT the argmax of `probabilities.calibrated`.

decoding.why: The model decides each 30-second epoch independently, which sprays isolated REM epochs into non-REM sleep: REM periods came out at 2.01x the expert count while total transitions were only 1.14x. A REM-targeted minimum-run rule removes those epochs and the spurious transitions they created.
decoding.selection: maximise (metrics improved - metrics degraded), subject to validation kappa not falling below argmax; ties broken by REM_Periods relative error
decoding.consumer_note: Through schema 1.0 the hypnogram was the argmax of these probabilities. From 1.1 it is not. Recomputing it by argmax will disagree with `hypnogram.predicted_stages`.

probabilities.calibration_note: Temperature scaling changes confidence, not decisions; argmax is identical before and after (asserted at build time). The DECODER, by contrast, does change decisions - see the `decoding` block.
probabilities.argmax_stages_note: argmax of these probabilities is NOT the shipped hypnogram; it differs on 17 of 1652 epochs in this recording.

Mean_Segment_Duration.reason: derived from run structure, which inherits per-epoch noise; mean relative error 32% on validation.

REM_Latency.reason: depends on a single epoch. Even on the decoded hypnogram it produced a false sleep-onset-REM reading - a narcolepsy red flag - on 3 of 31 validation nights (mean relative error 43%).

REM_Periods.reason: counts contiguous runs, so it tracks prediction fragmentation as well as physiology. Decoding moved it from 1.38x to 0.66x of the expert count; mean relative error 41%.

Segment_Duration_Variance.reason: derived from run structure, which inherits per-epoch noise; mean relative error 86% on validation.

Sleep_Efficiency.reason: aggregates over the whole night; per-epoch errors average out.

derived_metric_reliability.note: Only aggregate metrics survive per-epoch prediction error. Single-event metrics (REM latency) and run-structure metrics (REM periods, transitions) inherit it directly.

evidence_items.label: REM latency to first sustained REM period
evidence_items.definition: time from sleep onset to the first run of >=3 consecutive REM epochs
evidence_items.caveat: The decoder already enforces a minimum REM run, so this resolves to the same epoch as arch.rem_latency and is not an independent check. Its error (72.56 min) is measured against the expert's first SUSTAINED REM period while arch.rem_latency's (67.7258 min) is measured against the expert's first REM epoch - different references, so the two numbers must not be differenced. Both remain large against clinical thresholds.

evidence_items.label: N1 is low-reliability in this model
evidence_items.basis: representation-bound: no decision threshold improves N1 by more than +0.0086

limitations: Staging is from a single EEG channel (Fpz-Cz): the raw waveform plus 34 spectral features derived from that same channel. No EOG or EMG is used.
N1 is representation-bound: pairwise N1-vs-N2 AUC ~0.81, unchanged across every model variant, and no decision threshold improves N1 F1 by more than +0.0086.
Night-level confidence predicts agreement with the expert scorer, which is not the same as clinical correctness - both can be wrong on the same night.

The hypnogram is decoded with a REM-targeted minimum-run rule, so REM runs shorter than 3 epochs cannot appear in it by construction. A genuine brief REM intrusion would therefore be absorbed rather than reported. On validation the rule moved REM period counts from 2.01x the expert value to 0.83x - closer, but now slightly UNDER-counting, so REM fragmentation should be read as a lower bound.
No EOG or EMG is used. AASM scoring defines REM partly by eye movements and N1 partly by slow rolling eye movements, both of which are unavailable to this model.
